IsScalarOn XS XT v phi A s says that the majorant pairing satisfies <phi x, phi y> = s <x, y> for x in A and all y. idx is lidx at w: locLen(A, A meet B) - locLen(B, A meet B). l_w is lw = log N(w)/[K:Q] and e_w is ramw = v_w(p_w). The glued lattice is glueLat, the infimum over all finite places w of the localization at w of matLat(iota_{mu_w}, abelian2(mu_w)), with abelian2 t = matLat(P_t, M_t).

is-definite-rows: The plan reads this theorem as proving the definite-side condition. What it proves is the surjectivity and lower norm bounds at the selected bundles (eventually_norm_bound_of_more_points, eventually_L6_bound_of_lamLow) and the smallness parts w1, seeIso, pass (eventually_small_of_seeEx_primitive with indefinite_scale_theta_nonvanishing_alt); the rest is assembled by row_rRows_of_parts_alt. In the conclusion the lower norm bound is conditional on LeafUniqueMap (single row maps), which the proof does not use. The five published results are DiscreteSeriesCover, HarishChandraModules, CuspRapidDecay, CasselmanWallach and DiscreteSeriesClassification. Hypothesis (9) is proved along the linked parameters by Theorem is-definite-side-condition-holds (GlobalTheory.T.weil_unitary_entries'), which the assembly uses in GlobalTheory.Fc.S0.Open0ProofU.open_orbit_of_unramified_exponents_alt.

is-one-map-data: A summary of Formalism.IndefR.FWT.OMDat (a structure of about thirty fields: coefficient field c', the identification hV, lev, delta data, classes Cl' with lattices Lh, La and numbers Nc, gam, volumes, local constants ep, B, epF, the polynomial realization io with hw, phi, w, the unfolding data U2, dict2, xi, thAd, Plc), of OMDat.OneMapOf (EquivAt, OneMapTieC, PhRat) and of OMPins; the weight family kappa is WeightFamilies.Wt, the weight tie FWTie and the conjugation tie BarTie. is-onto-estimates: The conjunction of the statements used by ontoX_of_hypotheses_alt_alt and ontoX_of_twist_shares_exp_alt: runs_estimate_statement', rational_estimate_statement' (TwoRunsStatement, RationalityStatement'), ExportedStatement, MaximalityStatement (maximum_estimate_statement'), PageStatement, GeometricStatement', the rank (rank_at_twisted_places_of_max_geo with bigOn_comparison_at_twisted_places), TwistStatement', ShareStatement, BadPlacesStatement and ExponentStatement. Each is ForallRecordObjects or AtPtsAlt over the class FamHyp of standard families; EventuallyAtPoints also requires the point conditions (PointConditions'), and in ForallRecordObjects the scale may depend on the constants c (exists c0, for all c with c0 <= C and ConstBad c, EventuallyAtPoints ...). The record object of a point is OnObj (S2 p) (Mir (R2 p)) c, where R2 p = charOf p.R (F2 p) is the realization with the scalars of scalOf, F2 p is the level-2 face with the scale data p.Z, S2 p is its rows, and Mir is the product of the mirabolic subgroups mirabSub of GL_r(kP v) over v in R.Pg. The leaf predicates are stated in Definitions is-onto-page-estimates to is-onto-local-estimates. The proof follows ontoX_of_hypotheses_alt_alt; Steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 8 and 9, and the models of Step 7, are written from the is-onto-step lemmas, which state the local statements that the Lean assembles there (exists_runs_at_alt, twistedRational_R2_F2, exportSt, maxSt_alt, geoSt_of_pageSt_alt, rank_at_twisted_places_of_rec_span, modelSt_alt, badWSt_of_greenCuspidal_of_modelSt, expSt_of_alt). In Step 7, shareW_of_modelAt applies the two dimension statements T.definite_cuspForms_finite_regularRepresentation (Lemma is-onto-share-definite) and T.twoLevelFlagDomain_cuspForm_ranks_shifted_weights with T.twoLevelFlagDomain_eigenspace_share (Lemmas is-onto-share-ranks and is-onto-share-indefinite); the existence of the models is modelSt_alt (Lemma is-onto-step-models). Step 6 follows twistSt_of_alt and hasTwistBound_at: the twist condition is TwGood of FamHyp (via Des and WithTw), TwGoodAt at the place gives part (a) (I.Ok, whence isLatIn_eTh) and the parts IsLatIn, IdxAt and InclAt of (c) (PartBAt), with the numbers epsilon j b of (c); exists_leafTW1_of_twGoodAt takes epsilon'(v, j) = epsilon (j + 1) (sd v) and bounds the sum by sum_side_le and l_eq_plc. The tie at (v, j) is OnTie (TiedAt): t is toForms h fw j z, e_eq is t e_j = eOp t with eOp the good idempotent twisted by chi^-1 (as eGood of Step 8), ThJ_eq is Theta_J = t^-1(thetaBase R j P0 psi0^-1 1 v p) with p = ownAt D v, and X3_eq is X_3 = e_j t^-1(thetaTuple R j P0 psi0^-1 1 (mu v)). The export (ExportedStatement) is ExportTie = Reads: rd is semilinear for embW of the twist choice NChoice (whose DVR Oe is finite, injective and local over O_{i,k'}, and embW induces v by induces_embW), and spans rd(thetaBase) and rd(thetaTuple) are the spans of 1 (x) theta(a) and of incl(thPsi(a)), a in SgJ = Sigma_D(i, j, b), for the character chosenChar = phi^(b). TiedAt.lix_le transports Reads along t (Reads.comap) and applies Reads.lix_le, which takes M = O' (x) e Theta(Sigma) in IdxAt and then lix_le_of_read (Lemma is-onto-twist-transport); the lattice M_s(j) meet Z_g(j) is goodPartLattice_of_leafSup and e_j Theta_J(v, j) is a lattice by the rank (RankAtPlaces).

is-onto-step-rational: T.twistedClassSums_rational_of_rayClassFields, with hypotheses R.Char F, IoExt R, LUnif, OMPins, QGuard R, OneMapRowR with the phases 1, BaseLinks, RankRows and ContainsRayField (embK D) (tupLevel R t) for every t, where tupLevel R t = g 0 * g 1 * the product of the residue field cardinalities over R.Q t and ContainsRayField is the elementwise form in the statement. is-onto-step-kernels: IsKernel R i xi Q omega phi (a unitary chi with ChrEq chi xi, residue characters xiR with IsRes at the places of Q, a Weil datum for chrTh of the tuple (mu0, chi) and eta at level i + 1, and IsThPVecOf for the test vector); IsBaseKernel is IsKernel at delAt (plc v) and placesOver R (mu v) (ownAt D v). Theta_kappa(h) is seriesAt R i P0 psi0^-1 1 omega phi h, Theta_kappa is seriesSet (which asks h in GfC), the base theta lattice is thetaBase R i P0 psi0^-1 1 v (ownAt D v), and meeting the classes is MeetsClasses (dataLevel R i Q) h, which also asks h c in GfC. The trace with psi0 is levelTrace with psi = psi0^-1: levelTrace R i U psi is gaL of the coefficients D.what2.embLL ((psi g)^-1) on U and 0 off U, and D.what2.embLL is the embedding sigma_D of the definite-side datum, so the weights on P0 are sigma_D(psi0(g)). The other complex objects of the definition (the model of W_j, the lowest K-types, adForm) are taken at sg0 D A = sgAt D.what2.embLL A.v0, the embedding sigma_0 of the base place; for a realization the field RealDat.hv0 (A.v0 = InfinitePlace.mk D.what2.embLL) gives sg0 D A = D.what2.embLL (TraceIncl.sign_at_base_place_eq_embedding), so the two embeddings agree there.
is-onto-step-kernel-unique: T.baseThetaKernel_series_unique: BaseKernelUnique R i v (ownAt D v), the equality of singleSeries R i omega phi for any two base kernels. The hypotheses are Hk3.Core R F (the core conditions), v in R.twPl and R.tup_mu_on; the statement keeps all three, as the Lean states them, and marks them unused, since the proof uses none of them. The characterization gives all three (MaxSt.lean takes them from it). The Lean's points are Frame Psi r (a matrix for each tau in Psi), the flag domain is GG Psi Gm p0 with dmin the leading minors of gram and psgn the signs epsilon_i, Bor is the upper triangular group, lact and rmul the two actions; sections are IsSec, the norm is pnorm and bounded sections are IsBddSec. The constant term is fj la xi 0 P x: the integrality condition on nu is empty for nu = 0, periods la is generated by (m chiOrd(la) Re tau(a)) for real integral a, with chiOrd the chosen exponent of chi_fin, and the fundamental domain is the one chosen by h.choose. Cusp forms are SS la (IsIso xi: xi in Lambda, isotropic and nonzero). The majorant is maj = 2 posPart - Re hermC(v, v), with posPart through gramPos^-1; orthonormal is IsOrth; no contraction is NoContraction with OpNormLtOne. Weights are indexed by 0, ..., r-1 in the Lean; the book indexes them by 1, ..., r.
is-onto-share-two-level: TwoLevels E r U C: Psi, Gm, p0, xi0, comp : C -> DataX E r with comp_Psi, comp_Gm, comp_basePoint and comp_xi0, chi_one, Gamma_L', and tr with tr_herm, tr_Lambda, tr_L', tr_conj, tr_mul and tr_faithful. Families are M.SS la, u^*F is M.pull u F, S_kappa(M) is M.cusp la (the span of M.res of the families), and S_kappa(M)^{H, lambda} is BadCount.eig rho H lambda. Pulled back is IsPullRep. dimX, dimY, sOf and deMul (i < p0 in the Lean's indexing) are as in the book; ranks is ShareOn.Ranks M ka s ep c. The level hypothesis is LevelHyp = exists g, SplitsCompletely E g (g prime with [E:Q] primes of O_E containing it), 3r < g and UnipotentOver g, which quantifies over upper c = {gamma tr(u, c) : u c = c, gamma in Gamma_c}; M|_H is ShareOn.sub M H. The archimedean condition is ArchOn M ka T: ka = Fp + T L with GapsGe p0 L 1, PairGe L (1.9 T), GapsGe p0 (Fp - kLog - (dimY + 2) L) 0, PairGe (Fp - kLog - (dimY + 2) L) 1 and ArchOne (comp c) L Fp T for every c. ArchOne X L Fp T is: there is Xa : ArchInM X with Xa.L = L, Xa.Fp = Fp, Xa.T = T, Shares.Margins X Xa and a FlatM X Xa. The book does not unfold ArchInM (sections w_k, et, th1, th2, thp, invariant functions ph and ps0, bounds and Levi form positivity), Margins or FlatM.
is-onto-share-majorant: The proofs follow the Lean. (1) is maj_nonneg, from Data.maj_pos: gramPos_posDef (Sylvester's criterion, which the Lean proves itself as posDef_of_lminor by a Schur-complement induction), the projection ppos with ppos_eq and Hf_eq_two_ppos, and the dimension count hnli for the negativity of the orthogonal part. In (2), the Lean's maj_rmul applies maj_transfer, which compares the majorants of two points under an isometry g carrying the span of the first p0 columns of one onto that of the other, with g = 1 and the span conditions from exists_colP_rmul_eq_sum; the book's uniqueness of the orthogonal projection is the computation inside maj_transfer. (3) is ortho_holds with FrameDegreeData.bOf = uOf * diagonal sOf, where uOf is uMat of the Gram matrix (uT_G_zero, gram_u_eq, dmin_prod, sgn_dOf_pos, ortho_bOf), and IW.orth_mem_dom = mem_dom_of_isOrth'. The rest as follows: (1) MajorantConjugateTransfer.maj_nonneg; (2) OrthogonalFrameDomain.rmul_mem_dom and MajInv.maj_rmul; (3) ortho_holds and IW.orth_mem_dom; (4) MajorantOrthFrame.maj_eq_sum_norm_sq_of_isOrth (ModeHalfA.maj_orth); (5) FlagDomain.definite_frame_leading_minors_sign, where the Gram matrix is epsilon N^*N, and the step key of DefiniteOpNorm.opNormLe_definite, which applies maj_transfer with the span conditions H1 and H2 (span_colP).

(2) is card_mul_finrank_eig_of_free for a subgroup Hb of H, with the trace of rho(h), h /= 1, vanishing by trace_rho_eq_zero_of_free.

is-onto-share-borel-weil: The Lean's BWPolyStatement: P holomorphic on {det /= 0}, IsTriEquivariant a P with natural exponents a (P(xb) = triChar a b P(x) for invertible upper triangular b), and the conclusion a homogeneous MvPolynomial of degree sum a_i equal to P on GL_r(C). The Lean proves it (Closed.bwPoly = bwPoly_holds, from lemmaH_holds, L2DbarEstimates.ext and onePolyGrowth_holds) by showing that P is a polynomial along lines and then extending; the book cites the Borel-Weil theorem, by which such P are matrix coefficients of a polynomial representation of GL_r.

The slice statement is section_slice_eq_poly_div_det_pow (T.frameSection_slice_eq_poly_div_det_pow), proved for every section by Closed.bwPoly applied to y -> P(update x tau y) det(y)^N.

is-onto-share-trace: SmallElement.trace_sub_mem, for IsTotallySplitPrime E g (g prime with [E:Q] primes over it, obtained from SplitsCompletely by isTotallySplitPrime_of_splitsCompletely). The hypothesis on gamma is OpNormLe with constant e^{1/(3r)}, whose square is e^{2/(3r)}. The decomposition is ortho_holds with maj_rmul and ModeHalfA.maj_orth; the bound for sigma outside Psi uses map_conj_mulVec and normSq_star; e^{1/3} < 2 is sb_exp_third_lt_two; the operator norm is bounded by sb_normSq_mulVec_le.
is-onto-share-semistable: SemistableStatement for a HermForm S (an involution c with sigma(c x) = conj(sigma x) and G with c(G_ab) = G_ba; S.h x y = sum c(x_a) G_ab y_b), IsLattice and IsSelfDual. A Majorant has posDef, major (H sigma (G^sigma)^-1 H sigma = G^sigma) and conj_compat; IsSemistableZero uses latDeg, the log of the relative index minus half the sum of the logs of the real parts of the Gram determinants. The Lean proves it as Closed.semistable = semiContract_holds semiPoint degAdd (SemiPointStatement and DegAddStatement). The book's proof of (2) is semiContract_holds: sc_kerfam and sc_imfam (the families b and c in L), sc_append_li, sc_rank_pos, sc_index (the equality of indices), sc_gram_lt (the Gram determinants, through the Schur complement C' and detlt) and degAdd. The proof of (1) follows Closed.semiPoint = semiDeg_holds degAdd = SemiPt.semiPoint_of: detG_ne_zero (with no_line), wittBasis_holds, the transported lattice Lp = L.map (matLin P^-1) with formM_change, the graded pieces Gr j = (Lp meet cutSub (j+1)).map (projGe j) with exists_at, the weights dd j of adapted_semistable, the induction of adapted_semistable through flag_base and flag_step (P1, P2, P3) with hGb (rankOne_le_zero), hGt (pair_int, top_le_zero) and hGm (mid_supp, mid_int, mid_le_zero), exists_adapted_majorant with latDeg_transport, and latDeg_L_nonneg (gram_det_majorant, selfDualIndex_holds). The book's indices run from 1 to r; the Lean's Fin r runs from 0, so its cutSub e is the book's V_e and its projGe e is the book's pi_e.
is-onto-semistable-basis: LatDegBasisStatement, proved as latDegBasis_holds: exists_smul_le_span (the element D), the matrices M and Dm, det_gramC_comb, relIndex_span_comb (the index of the span of the columns of an integral matrix is the absolute norm of its determinant, through Module.Basis.span and LinearMap.det) and sum_log_normSq (the product formula). The Lean states it for positive definite H_sigma and any two families with IsKBasisIn.
is-onto-semistable-det: (1) is AbsDetStatement = absDet_holds = sdd_absDet, (2) is sdd_det_mono. Both factor A = B^* B (sdd_factor) and bound the eigenvalues of (B^-1)^* C B^-1 through the eigenvector basis (sdd_det_abs_le_one, sdd_det_ge_one).
is-onto-semistable-volume: (1) is IntegralIndexStatement = integralIndex_holds, (2) is SelfDualIndexStatement = selfDualIndex_holds, both through SemiDegIdx: the coordinates are coordLat B b with coordForm S b (spanIdx_eq_vecIdx, coordLat_integral, coordLat_selfDual), the decomposition X = sum C_i z_i is lattice_split (proved in the Lean by induction on k, with consZero; the book cites the Hermite normal form), the ideal J of split_norm is the product of cF i, the span of det G and CF i, with split_integral for J <= 1 and split_selfDual for 1 <= J, and absNorm_mul_relIndex_one for the norms. The Lean's (2) is stated for any K-basis b in L; when det Gram = 0 it holds trivially (vec_selfDual_bound). The ideal J is the volume ideal of the Hermitian lattice.
is-onto-semistable-witt: WittBasisStatement (S.G.det /= 0 implies P, m, g with P.det /= 0, 2m <= r, (P.map c)^T G P = wittMat r m g and the anisotropy of the middle part), proved in the Lean as wittBasis_holds through wa_main, by splitting off hyperbolic planes one at a time and diagonalizing the anisotropic rest. wittMat r m g has 1 at (i, j) with i + j + 1 = r and i < m or j < m (0-based), and g i on the diagonal for m <= i < r - m. g_fix and g_ne_zero give g^c = g and g /= 0. The published statement is the Witt decomposition of a nondegenerate Hermitian form over a field with involution in characteristic 0 into hyperbolic planes and an anisotropic part, together with the existence of an orthogonal basis of the anisotropic part; the Lean's statement is that decomposition written in a basis, with the hyperbolic pairs placed at the coordinates a and r + 1 - a. When c is the identity, K is totally real and the statement is the Witt decomposition of a quadratic form.
is-onto-semistable-graded: (1) is GradedExtStatement = gradedExt_holds (with latDegBasis_holds and degAdd): the lift c of b1 (hlift), sdd_append_li, sdd_append_span, sdd_satSub_eq, sdd_index and sdd_gram_step (sdd_schur for Q = E^* D E, sdd_cut_quad, sdd_det_mono). The Lean states it with diagMet delta for any K-bases b, b0, b1. (2) is flag_step. The empty family has degree 0 by latDeg_zero_fam.
is-onto-semistable-line: (1) is latDeg_single with gramC_single and sum_log_single; (2) is rankOne_le_zero, whose case of at least two vectors is excluded by linear independence and whose rank one case is latDeg_le_of_le with latDegBasis_holds and kBasisIn_single.
is-onto-semistable-pair: top_le_zero, for Gj, Gp with IsAt j and IsAt p, the pairing hypothesis hpair and delta j = d, delta p = d^-1: the form is hypForm S j p (hypForm_h), the index is spanIdx_pair (relIndex_sup_proj with projGe and projLt), and integralIndex_holds is applied to T = Gj + Gp with the basis x0, y.
is-onto-semistable-middle: mid_le_zero, for the form midForm S m g hfix (diagonal g on the middle coordinates); the Gram determinant is nonzero by the anisotropy (haniso), integralIndex_holds gives the index bound, and absDet_holds with quad_eq and quad_diag compares the Gram matrices at each embedding.
is-onto-semistable-majorant: exists_adapted_majorant (H sigma = ((P^-1).map sigma)^H * diagMet (adMet r m g dd) sigma * (P^-1).map sigma, with the identity wittMat^sigma D^-1 wittMat^sigma = D of wittMat_map_mul and wVal_adMet), and latDeg_transport for the degrees. adMet r m g dd is dd i for i < m, (dd (rev i))^-1 for i >= r - m and |sigma (g i)| otherwise (0-based).
is-onto-share-degree: DegAddStatement, proved as degAdd_holds: DegAdd.indep_parts, DegAdd.index_split (the product of the relative indices), DegAdd.relIndex_ne_zero_of_fg and DegAdd.log_det_gram_append (the Schur complement, Matrix.det_fromBlocks₁₁, with gramC_posDef). The Lean's deg is latDeg H B b, with relIndex for the index, and the quotient degree is quotDeg H L b c with quotGramC; L_b is satSub L b. The Lean takes the real parts of the determinants, which are positive reals here.

Only (1) is used in this chapter (Definite.free_of_definite). The proof of (2) follows the Lean: hss.2 for span {v} with relIndex 1, sum_eq_two_mul over the embeddings, Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos and maj_eq_hq. The form is MajorantOrthogonality.pform X (complex conjugation, G = Gm^t) with isLattice and selfDual; the basis is BallExPf.exists_frame with gram_iff; the majorant is maj_eq_hq; the embeddings outside Psi use conj_mem_iff, conj_compat and hq_conj.

is-onto-share-sections: (1) is the part on SS of siegelSpaceAlgebra_holds = BoundedSectionAlgebra.siegelSpaceAlgebra_of moderateCoefficientPositivity_holds coefficientConvolution_holds; the Lean statement also covers the spaces SSgt. (2) is FourierCoefficientDomain.isOpen_dom and flag_domain_frames_connected. The Fourier-Jacobi coefficient is Data.fj la xi nu P x (the condition on nu is the integrality on X.periods la; the fundamental domain is chosen). The proof of (1) follows siegelSpaceAlgebra_of: bdd_zero, bdd_add, bdd_smul, fj_add (with integrableOn_fj, through dmin_flow_real and nfac_flow_real), fj_smul, bdd_mul (bchar_add, chi_add, nfac_add) and fj_mul_zero; its two inputs, ModerateCoefficientPositivity (only its first clause, through sign_of_bdd) and CoefficientConvolution, are Lemma is-onto-sections-fourier. The proof of (2) follows flag_domain_frames_connected: P from X.signature, Ok p0 y for positivity of diagonal(sv) * Gy, mem_dom_of_ok (lead_pos, det_ne_of_ok), isPreconnected_ok (isPreconnected_det_ne on the block diagonal set V, ok_of_blk, the path mask with mask_eq, cross_zero and ok_mask), isPreconnected_upper for B^Psi, rmul_mem and orthonormalFlagTranslate_holds for the orthonormal translate.
is-onto-sections-fourier: The coefficient is Data.fj la xi nu P x. (1) is the first clause of ModerateCoefficientPositivity and (2) is CoefficientConvolution (a HasSum over nu' in Psi -> R). The Lean states both for sections of moderate growth, pnorm la P x <= C la1(x)^(-A) on the flag domain, and proves them itself (moderateCoefficientPositivity_holds, which identifies the coefficient with a Fourier coefficient on the torus R^Psi / periods by FlowMeanContinuity.fj_eq_fourCoeff; coefficientConvolution_holds through PeriodLatticeMembership.coefficientConvolution_of_subCoefficients and SublatticeCoefficients.subCoeff); bounded sections have moderate growth with A = 0 (mod_of_bdd), which is the case the book states and the only one used (sign_of_bdd, fj_mul_zero). ModerateCoefficientPositivity also has a second clause, a decay bound for the coefficients, not used here. The published statements are Shintani's theory of Fourier-Jacobi expansion for holomorphic automorphic forms on U(2,1), in the form of Murase and Sugano [MS02, 1.9 and Lemma 1.11(i)]: the coefficient f^m of the expansion along the centre of the unipotent radical vanishes unless m is totally nonnegative; and Lan's Fourier-Jacobi expansions for PEL-type Shimura varieties [Lan13, 7.1.2]. Those are stated adelically, or on Shimura varieties, at a cusp, for automorphic forms; the Lean's coefficient is the Fourier coefficient of s -> P(phi_xi(s) x) along the centre of the unipotent radical of the stabilizer of the isotropic line of xi, over the period lattice Pi_kappa, at a frame x of the flag domain, for any signature (p0, r - p0). The convolution (2) is the multiplication of Fourier series on the torus R^Psi / Pi.
is-onto-share-interpolation: LiftInterp.comp_interp, as used in exists_form_one_lift (T.exists_cuspForm_nonzero_at_one_lift) with G = M.upper c, the set Gamma°_c, through T.exists_upperLevel_subgroup_component, the prime g of T.exists_totallySplitPrime_upperLevel_unipotent and T.upperLevel_isUnitaryStabiliser_both_lattices. The Lean's comp_interp is stated for any group G containing Gamma whose elements preserve h, L' and Lambda and are unipotent modulo the primes over g; the book states the instance it is used for. The rest of exists_form_one_lift (the family u supported at c, and the vanishing of the translates through tr_faithful) is in the proof of Lemma is-onto-share-translates. The proof follows comp_interp. The definite case is T.upperLevel_trivial_definite_noContraction = DefiniteLevel.eq_one_of_definite (smallUnipotentUnitaryElementIsOne_proof with maj_mulVec_of_definite and maj_nonneg) and T.exists_detPowerSection_ne_zero_definite = DefConst.exists_ne_zero, with P = detPow Psi a (pnorm_detPow through the telescoping of the leading minors, not_iso for the absence of isotropic vectors, detPow_mem_SS). In the indefinite case the transport by b is rmul and lact_rmul with the B^Psi-equivariance (hP.1.1.2.1, bchar_ne_zero) and MajInv.lact_mem_dom; the free ball is T.freeBall_noContraction_unitaryUpperLevel (Lemma is-onto-step-free-ball-exists) and the orbit interpolation is T.orbitInterpolation_detWeight_freeBall_indefinite (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation), applied with G = M.upper c and M.chi_one c. The family of exists_form_one_lift is in the proofs of Lemmas is-onto-step-bad-weight-regular-one-lift and is-onto-share-translates.
is-onto-step-free-ball-majorant: ReciprocityTheory.MultiplicativeHeights.boundedBall_holds, the statement BoundedBallStatement (hq H u is Re(u^* H u), normSq, posSq and negSq the squared norms of u, u_+ and u_-, signMat p r the matrix J). is-onto-step-free-ball-bound: (1) is rhX_eq_sum_log, rhX_nonneg and rhX_rmul. (2) is GlobalTheory.Up.BallExPf.frame_bound with ballRatio r = (1 + 1/(7r)) / (1 - 1/(7r)), and sb_ballRatio_le for beta_r <= exp(1/(3r)); the proof follows frame_bound and norm_bound (hcs, the matrix H = (g^-1)^H g^-1, hJw, hDw, b1, b2, b5, and boundedBall_holds twice through hq_ct_mul).

is-onto-step-orbit-situation: The hypotheses of T.orbitInterpolation_detWeight_freeBall_indefinite: X : Data E r (items (1) to (6) of the flag data), (forall la, forall gamma in X.Gamma, X.chi la gamma = 1), IsOrth X x0, FreeBall X G x0 (1 / (49 r^2)), 0 < p0 < r, Even s and 2 r + 50 r^2 (|Psi| p0 (r - p0)) + 1 <= s; the weight is deMul Psi r p0 s.

is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-w: GlobalTheory.MinorRatioNear.minorRatio_near, for the function x |-> prod over tau of norm(dmin Gm x tau p0) / norm(lminor ((mat x0 tau)^-1 * mat x tau) p0)^2, written out in the Lean statement; division by 0 is 0 in the Lean, whence the reading of q. The proof follows minorRatio_near through exists_block_det_ge. The bound for the entries of g_0^-1 R is the one in the proof of Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-count (PoinPf.Kc_entry); here the Lean proves it again as norm_entry_le_one, through signed sums of rows, and the book follows that proof.

GlobalTheory.kaFrame_of_delta, with delta for q and bb for nu. The Lean asks delta >= 0 everywhere and delta measurable; the book takes q with values in [0, infinity). The sum in (3) is a tsum in [0, infinity] of ENNReal.ofReal (sqrt (kappa (gamma x))), bounded by a finite C.

GlobalTheory.kaFrame, an implication from three statements to the existence of kappa for every r, X, orthonormal x0 with PropDisc X and bb > 4 |Psi| r^2; orbitInterp applies it to the proved statements FramePotential.frame_potential_basic, MinorRatioNear.minorRatio_near and FrameSumBound.frame_sum_bound grpSep. GlobalTheory.grpSep has the statement of PoinPf.sep (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-count-separation), with (mat x0 tau)^-1 * gamma^tau * mat x0 tau in place of gM X x0 (lact gamma x0) tau, which is the same matrix as lact gamma x0 is gamma^tau x0 by definition; it is proved again, through proper discontinuity at (x0, x0) in the coordinates x0 (1 + M), and the book cites the lemma. FrameSumBound.frame_sum_bound is not the statement of part (3) of Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-count (PoinPf.kaSum): it is an implication from the separation statement for all data, and it bounds the sums of (prod over tau of |d_p0(gamma x)| / |l_p0(x0^-1 gamma x)|^2)^s, where kaSum bounds those of exp(-s rhY). The book follows its proof, which applies sumBd_sum (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-count-sum) to the matrices x0^-1 gamma x reordered by swapIdx, without the complex conjugation that kaSum applies.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-p: GlobalTheory.Up.IsPole X G x0 kappa eps C delta psi: psi (lact gamma (rmul x b)) = psi x for gamma in G, x in X.dom and b in Bor; psi <= 0 on X.dom; for every orthonormal x1, psi o cpt x1 is smooth on OmF x1 and -(kappa leviRh x1) <= leviO x1 psi; psi x <= dimX log (rhX x0 x + delta) + C when rhX x0 x <= eps; and -C <= psi x when eps / 2 <= rhX x0 x <= eps. dim X is GlobalTheory.Up.dimX. The Lean allows every real delta; the book asks delta > 0, the only case used.

GlobalTheory.Up.PoleEx, proved by PoleExistence.poleEx_holds = poleEx_of_rhTr PotentialTransfer.potential_transfer. The same statement. The proof follows poleEx_of_rhTr, with the potential transfer RhTr (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-pole-exists-transfer) and the nonnegativity of the Levi form of rhF from the gradient bound (Up.leviRh_nonneg, Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-solve-levi).

GlobalTheory.exists_cutoff_log_sharp, for rho0 > 0 and theta > 1: eps and C with 0 < eps < rho0, and for 0 < delta <= 1 a function g : R -> R, ContDiffOn R infinity on Ioi (-delta), with the four properties and deriv g, deriv (deriv g). The book states g on (-delta, infinity), where it is smooth; only its values on [0, infinity) are used. The step eta is GlobalTheory.exists_smooth_step_sharp_slope (rho0, eps), built from a ContDiffBump.

Two Lean lemmas: GlobalTheory.PoleExistence.exists_block_det_ge' (c < 1, the lower bound, with norm (n - 1) a b <= delta) and GlobalTheory.OrbitSum.exists_block_det_le (the upper bound 2), each for g * sgnMat r p * g^H = sgnMat r p, with the minors written as determinants of submatrices. The book takes the smaller of the two numbers delta. Both proofs are that of MinorRatioNear.exists_block_det_ge (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-weight-near), with exists_det_ge and exists_det_le_two in place of exists_det_near_one.

(1) is GlobalTheory.Up.rhX_lact (rhX x0 (lact gamma x) = rhX (lact gamma^-1 x0) x for IsUStab gamma), through rhX_lact_lact, with isOrth_lact_of_isUStab and MajInv.lact_mem_dom; the Lean states it for all frames x0 and x, where rhX is given by its formula. (2) is GlobalTheory.Up.FreeBall.unique. The book's elements preserving h are the Lean's IsUStab, which also preserve Lambda; only h is used.

GlobalTheory.PoleExistence.rhX_lower, for x in X.dom and t > 0: eventually for y near x, y in X.dom implies rhX x2 x - t <= rhX x2 y for every orthonormal x2. The orthonormal case is rhX_lower_orth. The same statement.

GlobalTheory.SharpGradient.SharpAt phi x xi: ContDiffAt R 2 phi x, 0 <= phi x, 0 <= Re leviV phi x xi and normSq (sum over j of wd j phi x * xi j) <= phi x * Re leviV phi x xi, with wd the Wirtinger derivative d/dz_j.

(1) is ReciprocityTheory.L2DbarEstimates.H.leviChain (LeviChainStatement), for v of class C^2 at x and k of class C^2 at v x. (2) is GlobalTheory.SharpGradient.sharpAt_ball, for g : Fin m -> V n -> C with ContDiffAt C 2 (g i) x. (3) is sharpAt_sum and sharpAt_sum' (sums over Fin m and over a finite type). (4) is SharpAt.of_minorant, with psi <= phi eventually near x and phi x = psi x.

GlobalTheory.Up.RhTr, proved by GlobalTheory.PotentialTransfer.potential_transfer: for orthonormal x1 and x2, ContDiffOn R infinity of z -> rhX x2 (cpt x1 z) on OmF x1, and at every z in OmF x1 its nonnegativity, leviO x1 (rhX x2) z xi = leviRh x1 z xi and the gradient bound with leviRh x1. The same statement. In the proof, the graph matrices are topT, lowT and graphT, and Hadamard's inequality is SharpGradient.det_le_prod_diag, which the Lean proves through the AM-GM inequality RgB.amgm; the book cites Horn and Johnson.

GlobalTheory.PoleExistence.poleFn X G x0 rho0 k: k (rhX x0 (lact gamma x)) for a gamma chosen among those in G with rhX x0 (lact gamma x) < rho0, and 0 if there is none, for every frame x, with k : R -> R. The book takes k on [0, infinity) and sets psi_k = 0 off the flag domain, where no property of the pole function is asked; on the flag domain the two agree, by FreeBall.unique.

(1) is GlobalTheory.PoleExistence.poleFn_inv; (2) is poleFn_eq with gamma = 1, as in hone of poleEx_of_rhTr; (3) is poleFn_local, for a < rho0 and k u = 0 for a <= u, with eventual equalities near z for the functions w -> poleFn (cpt x1 w). poleFn_eq_zero is the step of the second case.

is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-g: ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.AR.Up.RhGradFStatement: normSq (sum over j of wd j rhF z * xi j) <= (|Psi| min p0 (r - p0)) Re leviV rhF z xi, with wd the Wirtinger derivative d/dz_j, for orthonormal x0 and z in OmF x0; proved by RhGradFStatement_holds. Its hypotheses are an orthonormal x0, BlockConst X la, eps > 0, bb >= 0, bb + kappa < m and the curvature inequality at x0 with leviRh, leviO (phla la) and leviDens; its conclusion gives chi continuous with the stated values and M < infinity in [0, infinity], and for every delta and every psi with IsPole an F holomorphic on OmF x0 whose integral for muF, with the factor 1 / kaF x0 bb = e^(bb rho), is at most M. The proof follows poleSolve: the Levi form of the weight is nonnegative through Up.leviRh_nonneg, which comes from the gradient bound (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-solve-levi), and the exhaustion eF through ExF.levi_rhF_nonneg (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-solve-chart).

GlobalTheory.Up.leviRh_nonneg = OntoB.levi_rh_nonneg RhGradFStatement_holds: 0 <= leviRh X x0 z xi for orthonormal x0 and z in OmF x0. The conclusion is also part of Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-solve-chart (ExF.levi_rhF_nonneg), proved there through a minorant; the Lean proves it again from the gradient bound, and the book follows that proof where the Lean uses it, in the proofs of Lemmas is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-solve and is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-pole-exists.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-n: GlobalTheory.SharpGradient.rhF_le_near_zero, with the sum over Ent X of the |z_e|^2 for the mixed entries (b < p0 <= a in the Lean's indices from 0). rhF_sharp_gradient, which polePoint_holds cites, adds rhF >= 0 on OmF x0 (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-solve-chart) and the inequality |d rhF|^2 <= rhF leviRh, which polePoint_holds does not use.

ReciprocityTheory.L2DbarEstimates.Y.ap_local_blowup, with the same mean value hypotheses as ap_prod_blowup (proved as L2DbarEstimates.mv and mvInt). The same statement.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-p: GlobalTheory.Up.PolePoint, proved by polePoint_holds. The integral is over ball 0 rho for muF X x1, that is over the z in OmF x1 with |z| < rho with the density D_x1, and u is asked holomorphic on ball 0 rho cap OmF x1. The same statement.

is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-a: GlobalTheory.Up.OrbitInterpolation.exists_approx. Its hypotheses include the proved statements NfacRmulStatement, NfacLactStatement, PnormInvStatement, ExtFStatement, MeasInvStatement, PoleEx, PoleSolve and PolePoint; the square integrability is InAt X x0 W bb F for W the indicator of X.dom of exp(-(phla la + 0)), which is the gauge W_lambda; the last bound is norm (P (lact g x0)) <= eta sqrt(kappa (lact g x0)) for g in G with g != 1. The same statement.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-i: GlobalTheory.Up.OrbitInterp, a Prop over all r, X, G, x0, la, rho0, bb and m, proved as orbitInterp from the proved statements listed in the proof of Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large. 1 <= dimX X is the book's dim X >= 1, PropDisc X the proper discontinuity, and the curvature hypothesis is stated with leviRh, leviO (phla la) and leviDens. The same statement.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-c: Not a single declaration: (GlobalTheory.DivisionVolume.margin_iff h0 h1 (deMul s) (s - 2 r + 2)).2 (OrbitInterpWeight.gapsPairing_deMul X h0 h1 hs), as used in OrbitInterpWeight.large (orbit_interp_small uses the copy gapsPairing_deMul'). margin_iff is an equivalence between the curvature inequality at all orthonormal points and GapsPairing X (la - kapW X) m; only the direction from GapsPairing is used. The proof follows it: gapsPairing_deMul is the step on the gaps; margin_iff rewrites the right side with the private leviWeight_sub_leviDensity_eq_lemma, which proves the case c = 0 of Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-density again, through FrameThetaCompare.curv_lin (linearity in the weight, from Lemmas is-onto-share-counts-section-transfer and is-onto-share-counts-section-diagonal(2)) and the private phla_kapW_cpt_eq_log_densF (the summation by parts); the book follows this route; then FrameThetaCompare.margin_of_gaps gives the bound through CurvMargin.curv_and_margin (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-curvature).
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small: T.freeBallCentre_interpolation_detWeight_smallSignature = Up.OrbitInterpSmall.orbit_interp_small, the case p0 (r - p0) <= 3, through orbitInterp_small (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small-interpolation), which repeats orbitInterp (Lemma is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-large-interpolation) with kappa_exists and PoinSumBound.poin_conv_bdd. The proof follows orbit_interp_small, and the book writes out the proof of orbitInterp_small as the Lean does. orbit_interp_small also assumes that chi_kappa is trivial on Gamma, and does not use it.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small-i: GlobalTheory.Up.OrbitInterpSmall.orbitInterp_small, with PropDisc X, IsOrth X x0, 1 <= dimX X, 0 < p0 < r, p0 (r - p0) <= 3, 0 < rho0, FreeBall X G x0 rho0, BlockConst X la, 4 (r - 1) <= bb, 0 < bb, bb + dimX X / rho0 < m, the curvature inequality and the hypothesis that bounded sections are cusp forms. The same statement. Its proof repeats that of orbitInterp line by line, with kappa_exists in place of kaFrame and PoinSumBound.poin_conv_bdd with sum_bound in place of PoinStatement; the book does the same.

GlobalTheory.T.exists_uniform_bound_lintegral_flagDomain_ball_case, proved by IntBall.intBall: when 0 < p0 < r, p0 (r - p0) <= 3 and 2 (r - 1) <= s, some I < infinity bounds the integral of exp(-(s rhF x1 z)) for muF X x1, for every orthonormal x1. The same statement. The proof follows intBall and IntBall.lintegral_lt_top.

GlobalTheory.UpCoordCompare: T is toEntries = coordOf (nFrame z), with nFrame = zFrame * leviFrame of ExhaustionFrames, and cpt x0 (toEntries z) = point x0 z (cpt_toEntries); (1) is coordEquiv and measurePreserving_toEntries; (2) is toEntries_mem_OmF_iff and rhF_toEntries, where U is ExhaustionFrames.Om, defined by the operator norm of zBlock (the block Y), and opNorm_lt_one_iff converts it into positive definiteness; (3) is GlobalTheory.T.lintegral_expRho_eq_setLIntegral_unitBallDomain (IntBall.lintegral_exp_muF_eq_setLIntegral_Om, through map_mu), stated for ExhaustionFrames.density and rho, which are D_x0 o T and rho_x0 o T on U (densF_toEntries, rhF_toEntries). The book states the three parts together.

(1) is GlobalTheory.IntBallMinorOne.schur_bound, for Z an m x 1 matrix with Re det(1 - Z^H Z) > 0, with norm_det_le_add_rankOne; (2) is GlobalTheory.IntBall.MinorLast.det_sub_bound, with vecMulVec (star (q * N)) (q * N) for (qM)^*(qM). The same statements up to this notation.

GlobalTheory.IntBall.density_mul_exp_le: density X x0 z * exp(-(s rho X z)) <= bnd X z for z in Om X, when p0 = 1 or p0 + 1 = r and 2 (r - 1) <= s, where bnd is the product over tau of gB p0 (zOf z tau) and gB is the product of colGram (blkW p0 w) k^-2 for k < r - 1. The positivity of the gamma_j is T.columnGramDeterminant_diagonalBlockUnitLower_pos, gamma_{r-1} = 1 is T.columnGramDeterminant_unitLowerBlock_last_eq_one, t <= 1 is T.detOneSubOffDiagonalBlockGram_le_one_ball, and the minor bounds are T.unitBall_leadingGramMinor_lower_bound_first and _last.

GlobalTheory.IntBall.block_fin: the integral of hB p0 over Low r -> C is finite when 0 < p0 < r and p0 (r - p0) <= 3, which are the cases of the statement; hB p0 is the indicator of the mixed entries of absolute value at most 1 times gB p0. The cases are T.lintegral_cutoffGramBoundMixedBlock_two_lt_top, _rankThree_lt_top and _rankFour_lt_top; the inequality (*) is T.flagGram_density_inequality_complex, the Gram minors are T.columnGramDeterminant_unitLower_three, and the shear is T.lintegral_update_sub_shear'. The finiteness of the integrals of (1 + |t|^2)^(-sigma) is Mathlib's integrable_rpow_neg_one_add_norm_sq.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small-o: GlobalTheory.T.orbitSum_exp_potential_uniform_bound, proved by OrbitSum.orbitSum_le; the hypothesis and the conclusion are integrals and tsums in [0, infinity] bounded by finite constants. The same statement. The proof follows orbitSum_le.

ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.AR.Up.IsFundSet X x0 FF: FF measurable, FF in OmF X x0, the injectivity, and the covering for muF X x0-almost every z. As the density of muF X x0 is positive on OmF X x0, this is almost every z in Omega(x0) for Lebesgue measure.

ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.AR.Up.fundSet_holds (FundSetStatement), proved by FundSetPf.fundSet_main, for orthonormal x0 and PropDisc X. The same statement. The Lusin-Souslin theorem is Mathlib's MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn.

(1) is GlobalTheory.Unfold.lintegral_unfold, with the hypothesis MeasInvStatement (proved as measInv_holds). Its statement differs from that of PairUnfoldPf.lunfold (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-measure(2)) by the interchange of the sum over Gamma with the integral; the Lean proves it again by the argument of lunfold, and the book derives it from that lemma and the interchange. (2) is GlobalTheory.T.lintegral_invariant_chartSet_le_mul_fundamentalSet = Unfold.lintegral_chart_le_mul_fundSet, with m in [0, infinity] at least the encard of the set of gamma. Lemma cv-returns-unfold states the same Lean declaration in the setting of Chapter 9; the book states it here for flag data.
(1) is GlobalTheory.OrbitSum.rhX_symm (through norm_lminor_inv). (2) is GlobalTheory.OrbitSum.harnack, whose constant K is |Psi| log 8. The same statements.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small-w: (1) is GlobalTheory.Up.OrbitInterpSmall.sum_bound for s = nu / 2 (the Lean states it for 2 (r - 1) <= s) and (2) is kappa_exists, for bb with 4 (r - 1) <= bb and 0 < bb; both ask 0 < p0 < r, p0 (r - p0) <= 3 and PropDisc X.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation-small-p: GlobalTheory.PoinSumBound.poin_conv_bdd: the first two conclusions of PoinStatement (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare), under the hypothesis that the sums of exp(-(bb / 2) rhX x0 (lact gamma x)) are bounded for orthonormal x, with 0 < bb in place of 4 |Psi| r^2 < bb. The proof follows poin_conv_bdd: kaY_eq_exp, kaSum_of, sumBall (the proof of PoinPf.sumBall_holds with kaSum_of in place of PoinPf.kaSum), ballB, locD, and the assembly of PoinPf.poin_of.
is-onto-step-orbit-interpolation: T.orbitInterpolation_detWeight_freeBall_indefinite = OrbitInterpWeight.orbit_interp_deMul, which splits on 4 <= p0 (r - p0) into OrbitInterpWeight.large and T.freeBallCentre_interpolation_detWeight_smallSignature.
is-onto-share-translates: IndependentTranslates E, with detTr u0 c x the determinant of (pull (h h') u0 c x). The proof follows TranslatesDet.independentTranslates: the points of existsBalancedFrameCMUnitary_proof (only NoContraction), the forms of exists_cuspForm_nonzero_at_one_lift (whose construction is Lemma is-onto-share-interpolation), the sum over Quotient.out of the orbits (ssSum, hsum, hrep), and detNeAt (tr_mul for the cocycle, ssLact for the invariance under Gamma, ht1 for t(1,c), the permutation sigma and Matrix.det_permute).
is-onto-share-indefinite: ShareEig.share_eig (T.twoLevelFlagDomain_eigenspace_share): mulH through cusp_exists, bddSec_pull and mul_mem_SS; S = sum lambda(g) rho(g^-1); Phi = pi of the codomain restriction of S after mulH; injectivity by eq_zero_of_det, pull_pull and pull_one; the second inequality uses the third clause of Ranks.
is-onto-share-counts: ShareRanks.compT with compX, for X = comp c and n = nd X (nd_comp: nd of a component is dimY). The upper counts are UpperModel.upper for kappa, and for kappa - delta_s after multiplying by u (mul_mem, indep_mul); for kappa + 2 delta_s after multiplying by a nonzero bounded section of the shifted weight (T.exists_nonzero_boundedSection_shiftedWeight) and T.card_independent_boundedSections_shiftedWeight_le. The lower count is T.lowerRank_cuspForms_detWeight_oneComponent. delta is Fl.delta of the flat model, and n >= 2 and 11 n^2 <= T are the fields n_ge and T_ge of ArchInM. The proof follows compX: the independence of products is indep_mul (eq_zero_of_mul_eq_zero with isOpen_dom and flag_domain_frames_connected), the products are mul_mem. The archimedean model is ArchOne (an ArchInM Xa with Xa.L = L, Xa.Fp = F, Xa.T = T, Margins and a FlatM); the flat model's cusp forms s k lie in SSgt L 0 (s_van), its base points are xs, and S_eq and xs_inj describe the common zeros. The three counts and the section w are Lemmas is-onto-share-counts-upper, is-onto-share-counts-section and is-onto-share-counts-lower.
is-onto-share-counts-model: ArchOne X L F T is: there is Xa : ArchInM X with Xa.L = L, Xa.Fp = F and Xa.T = T, with Shares.Margins X Xa and Nonempty (FlatM X Xa); these are the archimedean data, the margins and the flat model. ArchInM, FlatM and Margins take X : Data E r, the data (1) to (6) of the flag data; the lemmas on jets, the maximum, the absence of a positive maximum, the upper counts and the reduction assume only Data, ArchInM and FlatM, as their statements say. The definition lists the fields that the counts use: (1) i, g0 (g, with genus_even and genus_pos), c (c_pos), de (Delta), n_ge, T_ge, Tcg0 and i_pos; (2) w with w_van (in SSgt L 0, cusp forms whose Fourier-Jacobi coefficients of order at most 0 also vanish) and w_nz, ph with ph_inv (IsInvFn), ph_nonneg, p1 and p3; (3) et with et_sec, et_ne and p4, th1 (firstTheta_vanishes, firstTheta_ne_zero), th2 (secondTheta_vanishes, secondTheta_ne_zero) and thp (thp_van, thp_ne), written theta_0; (4) posL, where leviM X (phla X L) x0 z xi is the real part of leviV of z |-> phla X L (cpt X x0 z), and phla X L = -2 log nfac L, nfac being N_L; (5) the flat model FlatM: w0 (weightForm_vanishes), s (s_van), delta, xs (xs_mem), S_eq, xs_inj, w0_ne, coord and family_le_coords. The chart is Inst.cpt X x0 z = rmul x0 (nmat X z), with nmat X z lower unitriangular, its entries indexed by Ent X = Psi x {(a, b) | b < a}, so that n = nd X. lambda_1 is la1 = sqrt firstMinimumSq, with c tau = Data.c = 2 |tau(xi0)| and maj the majorant. Not listed: N as such, c1, a1, rr and their conditions, p2, the potential ps0 with its smoothness, its Levi lower bound and its weighted bound cfwM, posLde and posF of ArchInM; w_le, denom_le_family and s_le_w of FlatM; and the margins. The quotient Q_{T',f} is UpperShift.quotT, thetaFac times the square of the norm of f over sumSq to the power T' + n + 13/2 (QuotientMax.quot for T' = T); real division by 0 gives 0 where sumSq vanishes.
is-onto-share-counts-jets: (1) is LeadJets.jets for one base point, with T = e, a0 = e + 1 and t_j(z)_k = 1 if k = j and 0 otherwise, as exists_comb takes it; the Lean treats all base points at once. Its proof is the induction of the book through LeadJets.step, which takes the b_alpha from taylor_expansion_local_coordinates in the coordinates zeta = s/w0 and adds b_alpha / w0(y_j)^e (the dd of hsurj) to the coefficients of degree a. (2) is UpperModel.exists_comb: the coefficient vectors lie in C^(Fin delta x multiLt n (e + 1)), of dimension delta binom(e + n, n) by ManyForms.card_multiLt_succ, and a linear dependence gives the combination. Holomorphy on D_X becomes holomorphy on OmF X (xs j) through OntoB.hol_comp. exists_comb takes X : Data E r, an ArchInM X and Fl : FlatM X Xa, and no margins.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction: reductionTheory_holds proves MahlerCompactnessCriterion: for every r, X : Data E r (the data (1) to (6)) and epsilon > 0 there is a compact K in X.dom such that every x in X.dom with epsilon <= la1 x has lact gamma (rmul x b) in K for some gamma in Gamma and b in Bor. It is a form of Mahler's compactness criterion for the unitary group of h. The Lean proves it directly, and the proof follows reductionTheory_holds: a normal frame (exists_normal_frame), the reduced basis of IntegralBasisReduction.reduce (through redGram_holds, an LLL reduction), the finiteness of the types of bounded bases (HermitianLatticeMaps.ty, FiniteTranslateSets.TS_finite), exists_gl for two bases of the same type, Gamma_index for the cosets, and the entry bounds of CompactEntryBounds. The finiteness of the integers of E with bounded conjugates is Mathlib's NumberField.Embeddings.finite_of_norm_le (through Sh_finite), proved there from the bounded coefficients of minimal polynomials; the book cites the lattice property of O_E instead.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-lll: ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.AR.IntegralModuleBases.RedGramStatement, proved by redGram_holds; the statement is the same. The reduced basis is ReducedBases.T2.IsRed (size-reduced, |mu_ij| <= 1/2, and |b*_j|^2 <= 2 |b*_{j+1}|^2), weaker than the reduced bases of LLL82 (1.4)-(1.5), whose existence the book cites. The Lean proves existence in exists_red_of by LLL's termination argument without the algorithm: the potential (the product over k of the Gram determinants of b_1, ..., b_k) is bounded below on all bases (hlow_of, through the integrality of the Gram determinants of integer vectors and an antilipschitz bound for B), a basis within a factor 4/3 of the infimum is size-reduced (size_reduce), and a failure of the second condition would allow a swap lowering the potential by a factor below 3/4 (pot_swap, norm_swap_j). The bound |b_i|^2 <= 2^(i-1) |b*_i|^2 is LLL82 (1.7) for j = i; the Lean proves it as norm_sq_le_pow_gs. The remaining computations (gs_sq_ge, red_norm_sq_le, red_coeff_sq_le, coeff_bound) are those of the proof.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-lattice: RealPlaceEmbeddings: finite_int and free_int (Lambda is a finite free Z-module), linIndQ and spanQ_eq_top (a Z-basis is a Q-basis qb of E^r), card_qb (N = r [E:Q]), two_card_Psi ([E:Q] = 2 |Psi|, from cmType), span_real_embeddings_eq_top and span_embV, and linIndR (the real basis). The map u of the proof is Tm, from TraceIntegralBasis.VS (EuclideanSpace over the complex places, the mixed space of Mathlib for a field with no real places) to C^Psi; the spanning set is TraceIntegralBasis.bas, Mathlib's mixedEmbedding.latticeBasis, which is the lattice property of O_E cited from Neukirch.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-normal: MajorantNormalForms.exists_normal_frame: there is b in Bor with gram (rmul x b) = diagonal of sgn and maj x tau v = sum |((x b)_tau^-1 v)_a|^2. H is Data.Hf x tau u w = hermC (2 ppos u - u) w, with ppos the projection (ppos_colP, hermC_ppos_lemma_5), Hf_conj_lemma_7 for the Hermitian symmetry and maj_eq_lemma_4 (also Data.Hf_self) for H(v, v) = maj. hgram_posDef uses Data.maj_pos (Lemma is-onto-share-majorant(1)). exists_normal orthonormalizes through Mathlib's LDL decomposition (LDL.lowerInv, defined by Gram-Schmidt): B = lowerInv^T times diag((D_cc)^(-1/2)). gram_normal and maj_normal are the two last paragraphs. Lemma is-onto-share-majorant(2) to (4) give the same statement by another route, which the Lean does not use here.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-forms: QuadraticLatticeForms and its neighbours. q_y is Qy X y v = sum_tau c tau |(y tau)^-1 emb tau v|^2 (with Mathlib's inverse, 0 for a singular matrix; the book assumes invertible components). C_X is HermitianPsiBounds.Cinv. (1) G_y is Am X y g, the Gram matrix of Ly (embV g i) for ip; Am_posDef (through linIndR and Ly_injective) and quad_int. B_g is Bm X g. Bm_eq writes Bm = Am times the matrix of Sg in zbas, from ip_Sg (with hermC_normal for the formula of h_tau in an orthonormal frame), and det_Am_le gives det Am <= |det Bm| (in fact equality). (2) is herm_bound, through herm_bound_psi and sum_sq_le, for IsNormal y (invertible components with Gram matrix J). (3) is Qy_smul. (4) is CompactEntryBounds.comb_bound, through comp_le_Qy and t <= 1 + t^2.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-basis: IntegralBasisReduction.reduce, for y with IsNormal X y and the fixed basis g = RealPlaceEmbeddings.zb X (Module.finBasis); the book fixes g. Its proof is the book's: quad_int, Am_posDef, det_Am_le and redGram_holds, with f = eb.map g.equivFun.symm.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-types: HermitianLatticeMaps.exists_gl, for ty X f = ty X f'. The type ty f is the pair (herm Gm (f i) (f j)) and the Z-coordinates of (RingOfIntegers.basis E k) * f i in f. The proof follows exists_gl: phi is the Q-linear map of the Q-bases qb with phi (f i) = f' i (phi_f), E-linear by phi_omega and phi_smul, isometric by phi_herm (through hL and hR), mapping Lambda into Lambda (phi_mem) with inverse phi f' f (phi_phi); gamma is LinearMap.toMatrix' of phiE, and IsUStab is the conjunction of the isometry and x in Lambda iff gamma x in Lambda.
is-onto-share-counts-reduction-compact: CompactEntryBounds. (1) is det_ne_of_gram and entry_bound, through gram_eq_transpose_mul_map_mul_fundamental_domains (the Gram matrix is Y^T A^tau conj(Y)); the Lean states the bound for every Y with Gram matrix J and nonzero determinant. (2) is gram_stab (through hermC_stab and hermC_expand) and inv_lact. (3) is Kset R = {w | gram of each w tau is the diagonal of sgn and every entry has norm <= R}, compact by Kset_compact (closed through cont_gram', bounded) and contained in X.dom by Kset_sub (dmin is psgn).
is-onto-share-counts-maximum: UpperShift.mainT for an integer T' with the rate 0 < 4/g0 - 2c(T' + n + 6 + 1/2), which is cg(2T' + 2n + 13) < 4; its proof is exists_maxT. For T' = T the Lean has a separate copy, T.normQuotientThetaFlat_attains_sup_off_common_zeros = QuotientMax.main (exists_max, with the rate rate_pos), proved the same way. The proof follows exists_maxT: quotT_inv (pointwiseNorm_invariance_holds), quotT_contOn (BigB.pnorm_contOn), thetaFac_le and thetaFac_bdd (p4 and the bounds of the cusp forms th1, th2), quotT_near (sumSq_lower through VanishPf.lower_of_det, and the continuity of nfac), sat_open (ExtFPf.luData_of lu_holds after ortho_holds, then LUB.isOpen_sat), sumSq_far (family_le_coords, p3 and BigB.S_pos), quotT_far (p1, ModeHalfC.first_minimum_pos with BigB.lam_ne, and exp(beta ph) >= 1 + beta ph), reductionTheory_holds (Lemma is-onto-share-counts-reduction) and IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn on Kc minus U. Both copies take X : Data E r, Xa : ArchInM X and Fl : FlatM X Xa, and no margins.
is-onto-share-counts-no-maximum: UpperShift.no_pos_maxT for an integer T' and a section f (IsSec, not necessarily bounded); for T' = T the Lean has a separate copy, T.quotient_no_positive_max_off_common_zeros = QuotNoMax.no_pos_max, proved the same way. The proof follows no_pos_maxT: hlog writes log Phi through BigC.log_pnorm_sq, OW.sum_pnorm_sq and the identities phla_add_nsmul, phla_sub and phla_nsmul for phla, with n1 = i (g0/2); then QuotNoMax.no_localMax, which takes the direction xi from exists_dir and uses T.levi_log_sum_sq_fibre_zero_and_nonpos_at_max (LeviFibre.main: the Levi form of log sum |s_k|^2 vanishes along xi, and a C^2 function has nonpositive Levi form at a local maximum), and posL at z = 0. Both copies take X : Data E r, Xa : ArchInM X and Fl : FlatM X Xa, and no margins.
is-onto-share-counts-upper: UpperModel.upper (T' = T) and T.card_independent_boundedSections_shiftedWeight_le = UpperShift.upper_shift (T' = T + n + 4). Both assume X : Data E r (the data (1) to (6) of the flag data), Xa : ArchInM X and Fl : FlatM X Xa, as the statement does; the margins of an archimedean model (Shares.Margins) are not assumed. Both argue by contradiction: exists_comb with e = T' + n + 6, isBddSec_sum, exists_s_ne, exists_mul_ne (eq_zero_of_mul_eq_zero on the connected domain) and pnorm_pos, then the maximum (QuotientMax.main, resp. mainT with rate_shift) and the absence of a positive maximum (QuotNoMax.no_pos_max, resp. no_pos_maxT). The rate comes from Tcg0, T_ge and n_ge, as in rate_pos and rate_shift.
is-onto-share-counts-section: T.exists_nonzero_boundedSection_shiftedWeight = ShareSection.exists_bddSec_shift. The statement keeps the Lean's hypotheses; the proof discards the margins, the conditions GapsGe and PairGe on F - kLog - (n + 2) L, Even s, and u with hu and hu0. delta >= 1 is UpperModel.upper applied to thp * w k ^ T (BoundedSectionAlgebra.bdd_mul). The rest is InterpWeight.interp_weight for G = (n + 4) L - 2 deMul s and the values 1, which gives w in SSgt G 0 with w(xs j) = 1. Its hypotheses: hmar with bb = 4 |Psi| r^2 + 1 and m = 4 (1.9 T) - 2 T - 2 (r - 1), and hstr with eta = 1/2, from CurvMarginClosed.curv_and_margin_closed (block_fst, block_snd and cross for a = 4 and a = 3) and IW.leviM_comb (e4, e3), with size_le and card_mul_le_nd for 4 |Psi| r^2 + 2 r <= 2 T; hcusp from ThetaRecordCompare.cusp_of_gaps with gaps_G and pair_G; and ClosedDiscontinuity.propDisc_closed. The book's mu_a is a L - 2 deMul s - kapW and its k is kapW X. The proved statements that interp_weight takes as hypotheses (normFactor_rightBorel_holds and the others) are not mentioned in the book.
is-onto-share-counts-section-levi: phla X la = -2 log (nfac la) is phi_lambda; OmF X x0 = {z | cpt X x0 z in X.dom} is Omega(y); rhF and densF are rho_x0 and D_x0 (densF uses the minors dmin i.castSucc, i in Fin r, that is d_0 to d_(r-1)). leviV n g z xi = sum_(j,k) wd j (wdb k g) z xi_j conj(xi_k), with Wirtinger derivatives; leviM X g x0 z xi = Re leviV of g o cpt x0, leviO is leviM, and leviRh and leviDens are the Levi forms of rhF and of log densF. The Lean defines leviV for every function; the book's Levi forms are those of smooth functions, which these are on OmF (phla_cpt_cdAt, logDens_cdAt). Curvature constants (nu, m, eta) are the hypotheses hmar and hstr of InterpWeight.core, InterpWeight.interp_weight and LowerInterp.kron_at (with psi = 0): exists bb, m with 4 |Psi| r^2 < bb < m and m leviRh <= leviO (phla la) - leviDens - n leviO (phla L), and exists eta > 0 with 2 eta leviO (phla L) <= the same; nu is bb.
is-onto-share-counts-section-diagonal: (2) is T.leviForm_weightMetric_orthonormal_diagonal = LeviZero.leviZero = levi_phla_zero, the sum over Ent X with sgn p0 a * sgn p0 b * (la b - la a) |xi|^2 for b < a. (1) is LeviZero.leviV_Lm, a computation with jets of the minors (HasJet, det_jet_sq), whose condition b < i <= a is the book's b <= i < a after the shift of a and b to indices from 1. The book states (1) as a computation without its proof.
is-onto-share-counts-section-transfer: LeviTransfer.levi_transfer, for every x0 (not only orthonormal ones). It assumes KapGGStatement and the statements NfacRmul, NfacLact and PnormInv, which the Lean proves (FrameMeasureClosed.kapGG_holds, NormFactor.nfac_transform). The injectivity of D comes from KapGGStatement (det of the derivative of the change of charts is bchar (kapW X) b) and is not used in this chapter.
is-onto-share-counts-section-transfer-lu: LUStatement, proved by lu_holds (LUStatementPf, PfA, PfB, PfC). The Lean's Delta is DeltaF X x0, z(x) is zF X x0 x and b(x) is bF X x0 x = Lm (Mx x) * Mx x with Mx x = (mat x0)^-1 mat x; the density of {Delta != 0} is dense_delta. The Lean states (3) for z in OmF X x0 = Omega(x0) and b in Bor. The triangular factorization is Gaussian elimination; the Lean proves it itself (Lm, Lm_mul_up, Lm_unique, lminor_nb).
is-onto-share-counts-section-transfer-ja: KapGGStatement, proved by FrameMeasureClosed.kapGG_holds = UnitriJac.kapGG_of_det applied to det_conj_strictLower (the determinant prod B_aa^(2a - (r - 1)) for indices a from 0, which is the book's 2i - r - 1) and det_mul_strictLower_eq_one. The weight k is kapW X. The Lean's statement does not assume beta holomorphic; its proof obtains the derivative of beta through the adjugate (deriv_rel), as the book's proof does through the inverse.
is-onto-share-counts-section-curvature: The second part of CurvMarginClosed.curv_and_margin_closed, that of CurvMargin.curv_and_margin applied to T.leviForm_weightMetric_orthonormal_diagonal and levi_transfer. beta is CurvMargin.blockWt. The first part, CurvGGStatement (nonnegativity and positivity of Levi forms of weights with the same monotonicity), is not used here.
is-onto-share-counts-section-density: IW.leviM_comb (la1 la2 : Wt, k : Nat), stated for leviM of phla (la1 - kapW X - k la2); the book's k is kapW X and its c is the Lean's k.
is-onto-share-counts-section-gauge: A gauge is IsMetricW X la W (W : Frame -> ENNReal: measurable, W (rmul x b) = W x / ofReal |bchar la b|^2 and W (lact gamma x) = W x on X.dom); bounded below is WLower (c exp(-phla la) = c N_la^2); B-equivariant is IsBEq; square integrable is InAt X x0 W bb F, the integral of ofReal(|F|^2 / kaF bb) * W o cpt against muF, the Lebesgue measure on OmF with density densF, where 1 / kaF bb = exp(bb rho). The Poincare series is poin, a tsum, which is 0 for a family that is not summable; b^lambda is bchar.
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker: InterpWeight.core, which takes bb, m, eta and the proved statements NfacRmul, NfacLact, PnormInv, ExtF, MeasInv, VanishAtS and KapGG as hypotheses and returns P with P(lact 1 (xs j)) nonzero; and LowerInterp.kron_at, the same construction for la with an invariant function psi added to the weight, which the Lean uses with psi = 0 and which returns some gamma0 in Gamma (its proof takes gamma0 = 1) and bb existentially. The book states the case psi = 0.
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-p: The facts key in InterpWeight.core: KronAssembly.sec_ne_zero, Fl.S_eq, and OrbitCoord.det_fderiv_ne_zero_orbit (with KapGGStatement, proved by FrameMeasureClosed.kapGG_holds), which Fl.coord gives at the base points. The Lean writes the point as lact gamma (rmul (xs j) b).
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-g: KronMetric.kronMetric for psi = 0: W is the indicator of X.dom of ofReal(exp(-(phla la + psi))), and exp(-phla la) = N_la^2. The Lean proves it for every bounded invariant psi smooth in the charts, assuming the NfacRmul statements; the book states the case psi = 0 used here.
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-s: (1) and (2) are kronSolve with psi = 0; (3) is KronValue.value_and_integrability with delta = 2 eps, which assumes VanishAtSStatement (proved by GlobalTheory.vanishAtS_holds) and that w0 and the s k are bounded sections (kronSolve itself assumes only that they are sections). The statement has the Lean's hypotheses: 0 < nd X, 0 <= bb < m, 0 < eta, the two curvature inequalities only at x0 (for z in OmF X x0), and the positivity of leviO X x0 (phla X L) on OmF X x0, which Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker supplies from curvature constants and from (4) of Definition is-onto-share-counts-model (ArchInM.posL), as InterpWeight.core does. kronSolve also takes a function psi smooth in the chart, added to the weight; the book states the case psi = 0, the only one used here. The integral in (2) is the Lean's integral against muF with 1 / kaF bb = exp(bb rho); Real.rpow makes the integrand 0 where S = 0. The compact-set clause of (3) is over sat X x0 C.

VanishAtSStatement, proved by GlobalTheory.vanishAtS_holds through VanishAtSimpleZero.vanish_of_simple_zero, which is stated for functions on V n near 0; the book reads it in the chart at x1. The statement also assumes x1 in X.dom, which holds for orthonormal x1 (IW.orth_mem_dom); the book omits it.

Collects OntoB.isOpen_OmF, IW.zero_mem_OmF, OntoB.rhF_contDiffAt (rho is rhF X x0), OmFConnStatement_holds (IsPreconnected (OmF X x0), with nonemptiness from 0), ExF.rhF_nonneg, ExF.levi_rhF_nonneg and ExF.isCompact_subF (the sublevel sets of eF X x0 = rhF + log (1 + |z|^2) within OmF X x0). kronSolve uses them as stated here.

(1) is ExF.det_one_sub_mul_conjTranspose_mem_Icc, a private theorem of ExhaustFStatementPfE, which states that the real part of det(1 - Z Z^H) lies in [0, 1] and equals its norm. (2) is ExhA.det_mul_det_le_normSq_det, with the real parts of the two determinants on the left. Its determinant comparison is I.maDet, that is DetMonoStatement (B and A - B positive semidefinite give Re det B <= Re det A), proved by Bl.DetMonotoneStarMulSelf.det_mono; the book uses Lemma is-onto-semistable-det(2), which has the same proof, as 1 - Z Z^H is positive definite in (2).

The 'if' direction is ExF.mem_dom_of_gramPos, through ExF.psgn_dmin_le, ExF.psgn_dmin_gt and ExF.neg_of_perp'; the 'only if' direction is Data.gramPos_posDef (Sylvester's criterion, posDef_of_lminor), with the determinant condition from Data.mem_dom_iff. The matrix g_tau(x) is X.gramPos x tau. The Lean states the two directions separately and for Data, whose flag domain uses only Psi, the Hermitian matrix and p0.

N_tau(z), Y_tau(z), Z_tau(z) and R_tau(z) are ExF.n1, ExF.Wm, ExF.Zt and ExF.Am, built from ExF.nM X z tau = mat (nmat X z) tau. (1) is ExF.cd_Zt, which states that the entries of Zt are holomorphic (ContDiff over C); the book reads the polynomial form from its proof (the inverse of n1 is its adjugate). (2) is ExF.gramPos_eq with ExF.det_gramPos and leadingMinor_eq_gramDet. (3) is ExF.mem_OmF_iff. (4) is ExF.rhF_eq_sum, rho = - sum_tau log |det Am|, with ExhA.det_re_pos_im for the positivity of det Am; ExF.rhF_eq_log writes it with the real parts.

HE.hormander_open, the case of an open set U of C^n of ReciprocityTheory.L2DbarEstimates.hormander, which proves HStatement for an EtaleStein manifold (a Hausdorff second countable space with a local homeomorphism to C^n and a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion function). The Lean proves it itself, as F.hStatement_of applied to E.ap, E.tStarIbp, chain, C.reg and the mollifier lemmas B.moll_graph, B.moll_smooth, B.moll_support and B.kernel_std. Published form: Hormander's L^2 estimate [Hor65]; the form with a semi-positive curvature operator and the pointwise bound h is Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry (version of June 21, 2012), Chapter VIII: Theorem 4.5 (complete Kahler manifolds, A semi-positive, <A^-1 g, g> defined as the least alpha with |<g, u>|^2 <= alpha <A u, u>), Theorem 5.2 (a weakly pseudoconvex Kahler manifold, Definition 5.1, carries a complete Kahler metric) and Theorem 6.1 (the estimate for a non-complete metric such as the euclidean one). For the trivial line bundle with weight e^-phi and (n, 1)-forms g = dbar F0 wedge dz_1 ... dz_n, <A g, g> is the Levi form of phi, so <A^-1 g, g> <= h is the Lean's hypothesis, and F = F0 - f is holomorphic. The Lean's U has the smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion e, so it is weakly pseudoconvex.

ReciprocityTheory.L2DbarEstimates.ext (EXTStatement), proved through C.ext, where reg applied to extWeak gives a holomorphic U on the ball equal almost everywhere to the extension of u by 0, hence equal to u on the open set where g does not vanish. Published form: Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter VIII, Lemma 7.3 (d'' v = w across an analytic subset Y for v in L^2_loc, w in L^1_loc), here for v = u, w = 0 and Y = {g = 0}, with Chapter I, Corollary 3.30 (hypoellipticity of d'' in bidegree (p, 0)) for the holomorphic representative. If g vanishes identically on the ball, the Lean's statement holds trivially, with U = 0; Lemma 7.3 is for Y without interior.

HE.interp_euclid, for the cutoff HE.cut eps (a smooth bump around 0 with radii eps and 2 eps, values in [0, 1]); the book fixes such a function. nsq s is S, and the hypothesis that s k0 does not vanish identically on open subsets is hgn.
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-e: ExtFStatement, proved by extFStatement_holds = extF_of lu_holds FrameMeasStatement_holds. The set of z with c_x0(z) in C B is sat X x0 C.

FrameMeasStatement, proved by FrameMeasStatement_holds. The constant K is finite (K < top in ENNReal) and the integral on the left is over C for the volume on Frame = M_r(C)^Psi. The book treats it as a self-contained computation.
is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker-v: KronOff.vanish_off with psi = 0; Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-kronecker uses it with delta = 2 eps. Its hypotheses are those of the statement: 0 < nd X, x0 and x1 orthonormal, w0 and the s k sections of weight L, 0 <= bb, closedBall 0 delta inside OmF X x0, chi = 0 for |z| >= delta, IsBEq X la P with P o cpt X x0 = F on OmF X x0, the finite integral, x1 not of the form c_x0(z) b with |z| <= delta, and the conditions at x1. It also takes a continuous invariant function psi in the weight, used with psi = 0. It assumes MeasInvStatement, VanishAtSStatement and the NfacRmul statements, which the Lean proves.
is-onto-share-counts-section-discontinuo: PropDisc X, proved for every X : Data E r by ClosedDiscontinuity.propDisc_closed (propDisc_arithmetic_group_frames). The neighbourhoods are members of nhds x in Frame. The Lean's norm on C^r is the largest absolute value of a coordinate, as in the proof. The finiteness of algebraic integers with bounded conjugates is Mathlib's NumberField.Embeddings.finite_of_norm_le.
is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare: PoinStatement, proved by poin_holds = poin_of_inputs lu_holds PoinPf.sumBall_holds PoinPf.ff_holds. (1) is the summability of the norms, (3) the clause with IsFundSet and InFF, and (4) the bound with values in ENNReal, the supremum over z with norm < rho and cpt X x z in X.dom of (ofReal (exp (-phla la)) / W)^(1/2). Only (2) is used in this chapter.
is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-me: (1) is MeasInvStatement, proved by measInv_holds; the measure D_x0(z) dz on Omega(x0) is muF X x0, Lebesgue measure restricted to OmF X x0 with density densF. (2) is PairUnfoldPf.lunfold, which assumes MeasInvStatement and an LU datum at x0 (ExtFPf.luData_of lu_holds), with the fundamental set IsFundSet X x0 FF. The book treats (1) as a self-contained computation, as Chapter covolumes does for the same declaration.

(1) is SubMeanStatement, proved by PoinPf.subMean_holds; (2) is SubMeanLocStatement, proved by PoinPf.subMeanLoc_of lu_holds. B_rho(y) is Bset X y rho. The mean value inequality is L2DbarEstimates.C.mv (MVStatement, for a radial weight; here the weight 1). The Lean states (1) for P differentiable on X.dom, and (2) for P with IsBEq X la P.
is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-co: rho_Y is PoinPf.rhY X x0 and exp(-s rho_Y) is kaY X x0 s. (1) is lminor_gM_ne, kaY_rmul and kaY_cpt. (2) is PoinPf.ka_comp, for bb >= 0, in the Lean's form kaY X x0 bb (cpt X x w) <= exp(bb 3 |Psi| log 2) kaY X x0 bb x for every orthonormal x and every w with |w| < rho1, with no condition that c_x(w) lie in the flag domain; rho_Y is defined on all of M_r(C)^Psi with Real.log, which reads log 0 as 0. (3) is PoinPf.kaSum, through PoinPf.sep and sumBd_sum (the separated sum of products of |det D_k|^(-2s) over families in U(p,q)^f, for s > 2 f (p + q)^2). The Lean works with the matrices Mq, the complex conjugates of x0^-1 x reordered so that the indices p0 + 1, ..., r come first; the book uses x0^-1 x itself in (2) and passes to Mq in (3). Proper discontinuity is used only in (3).
PoinPf.sep. The Lean's matrix is gM X x0 (lact delta x0) tau = x0_tau^-1 (delta x0)_tau, and its proof uses the sup distance on Frame.

sumBd_sum, for families x : iota -> Fin f -> Matrix (Fin p + Fin q) with IsUpq (x a k), that is (x a k)^H Jf (x a k) = Jf with Jf = diag(1_p, -1_q), and the separation hypothesis as stated; the sum is a tsum in [0, infinity] of ofReal (prod_k (normSq det (x a k)_22)^-1 ^ s), and C is finite. SumBoundStatement_holds, for discrete subgroups, uses the same lemma but is not used here.
is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare-ba: SumBallStatement, proved by PoinPf.sumBall_holds. Its hypothesis is the Lean's Hyp, which also includes WLower (W bounded below) and the holomorphy of F on OmF X x0; the proof discards both, and the statement keeps them and says they are unused. Lemma is-onto-share-counts-section-poincare supplies them.
is-onto-share-counts-section-separate: Not one declaration of the Lean. The published result is local: under Kudla's splitting the stabilizer of a self-dual lattice acts on the characteristic function of the lattice through the characters at the determinants, trivially at a nonsplit place where they are unramified. The Lean proves the global form its own way: the pairs with the eigenvalue property form a closed subgroup (eigSub, by om_cont and the continuity of the characters); stabilizer pairs supported at one place generate the stabilizer pairs topologically (T.mem_closedSubgroup_of_localStabilizerPairs); at a place of P, of its conjugates or at another split place the scalar is computed from the Weil datum (T.splitPlace_weilRep_latticeVacuum_character, VecInv.om_latVac_split); at a nonsplit place outside P the vacuum is fixed (T.weilOperator_lattice_stabiliser_fixes_vacuum_nonsplit, VecInvInert.om_fixes_vacuum; compare Lemma th-nonsplit-vacua). (2) is T.adjointHalfDatum_stabilizerPair_move (AdjDatumMove.adjDatum_actO) for the level function adjDatum S T betaS betaT Pg Q xi a: zero unless IsHalf a x and frMapAdj x (= betaS^-1 G_S^-1 x^* G_T betaT) is integral, then omegaK Pg (top block 1, lower rows 0) times omegaQ Q r xi (-1) (xi(det top)^-1); the proof is red_actO, omegaK_mul and omegaQ_mul, as written. Each part carries only the Lean's hypotheses: in (2), a is any element of AE D (IsHalf a x is a * x = x, not a condition that a be idempotent), g and h need only finite parts in St beta, and there are no character psi, lattices, IsFrame or Weil datum; (3) has no adelic matrices and no eta-tilde; and psi in (1) and (3) is standard because the Weil datum includes IsStdChar. (3) is T.weilAction_schrodingerModel_finiteIdempotent (SchrMove.smul_om_eq), for IsThetaAt at a with c = 1, under IsWeilDatumO, IsSelfDualC for both lattices, a * a = a, infPart a = 0, the lattice condition (u in latO iff actO g h u in latO), IsThetaFunO f0, c /= 0, om (g, h) f0 = c f0 and the move of Phi; the conclusion is d * om (g, h) f = c * f. is-transference: Standard: the case i = M of Banaszczyk's transference theorem [Ban93, Theorem 2.1], which gives the stronger bound M^2/lambda^2. The Lean states it over Q (a rational basis b, a symmetric, positive semidefinite, nondegenerate rational form B, and the dual condition that B(u, b_j) is an integer for every j) and proves the weaker bound (M^2/lambda)^2 with its own argument: GlobalTheory.ShortVectors.transference_rat passes to a Euclidean model (exists_euclidean) and the dual basis, and applies ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.T0.transference_dual.
is-selfdual-classes: GlobalTheory.exists_finset_selfDual_classes_rootDiscr, from ClassCount.exists_finset_classes with B = 4 f^3 n^4 r_E^2 and bound_le for Step 4. The Lean's fdeg E is the degree f of the totally real subfield, and the bound is written with finrank Q E = 2f. Step 1 is RootClassCount.exists_bounded_basis: exists_short_vectors (the trace form traceHerm, its dual minimum trace_dual_min through the different, with absNorm_inv_differentIdeal and the mean inequality finrank_mul_abs_norm_rpow_le_sum, then transference_rat and two_mul_le_traceHerm), euclidean_basis_exists for the E-basis, and SelfDualClasses.norm_herm_le. Step 2 is pairings, range_le_pairings and vecMul_mem_of_pairings_le; the Lean's Hermitian form is linear in the first variable, so its module of pairings contains the row space of A, where the book's contains A O_E^n. Step 3 is ClassCount.exists_finset_types: the packing count PackingSeparation.count, norm_det_le_pow and natAbs_norm_le_pow for the determinant, card_quotient_range_vecMulLinear for the index, and exists_finset_submodule with BoundedBasis.exists_generators_mod_smul for the modules between the row space and O_E^n.
is-places-prime-sums-rs: No Lean counterpart. The Lean proves the three bounds as in the proof of Lemma is-places-prime-sums (primeBoundsExact). The bound theta(t) < 1.01624 t of [RS62] is stronger than the bound theta(t) <= t log 4 the Lean uses.
is-eigenvalue-numeric-direct: No Lean counterpart. The Lean groups the factors as in the proof of Lemma is-eigenvalue-numeric (UpperTheory.Mu.numeric_bound with GlobalTheory.lamLow_numerical_end).
is-vacuum-unkilled-splitting: No Lean counterpart. The Lean argues as in the proof of Lemma is-vacuum-genus-one(1): TwoTorsionPt.isTwoTorsionCMPoint_of_odd_multiple for existence and ThetaConj.two_torsion_unique for uniqueness.
is-vacuum-determinant-dual: No Lean counterpart. The Lean proves the identity locally, as in Step (1a) of the proof of Lemma is-vacuum-norm-bound (GlobalTheory.T.relDetIdeal_selfDual_normOne, through CharValCompare.normOne_detI).
